title: Triangles 3000
statementMd:
You are given a set $*L* = {*l*_{1}, *l*_{2}, ..., *l*_{*n*}}$ of $*n*$ pairwise non-parallel lines on the Euclidean plane. The $*i*$-th line is given by an equation in the form of $*a*_{*i*}*x* + *b*_{*i*}*y* = *c*_{*i*}$. $*L*$ doesn't contain three lines coming through the same point.

A subset of three distinct lines is chosen equiprobably. Determine the expected value of the area of the triangle formed by the three lines.

## Input

The first line of the input contains integer $*n*$ ($3 ≤ *n* ≤ 3000$).

Each of the next lines contains three integers $*a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*}$ ($- 100 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ 100$, $*a*_{*i*}^{2} + *b*_{*i*}^{2} > 0$, $- 10 000 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10 000$) — the coefficients defining the $*i*$-th line.

It is guaranteed that no two lines are parallel. Besides, any two lines intersect at angle at least $10^{ - 4}$ radians.

If we assume that $*I*$ is a set of points of pairwise intersection of the lines (i. e. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/de097575c69058d4f91ea475f9e4590eabe69d2e.png)), then for any point ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/dc54b15ea9c105831ed892dd178fd6d69a00e235.png) it is true that the coordinates of $*a*$ do not exceed $10^{6}$ by their absolute values. Also, for any two distinct points ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e1cf69a80b39fbbb83f4c93698169310a026635e.png) the distance between $*a*$ and $*b*$ is no less than $10^{ - 5}$.

## Output

Print a single real number equal to the sought expected value. Your answer will be checked with the absolute or relative error $10^{ - 4}$.

## Note

A sample from the statement is shown below. There are four triangles on the plane, their areas are $0.25, 0.5, 2, 2.25$.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/83dbaa02f0f16b09fdd2a6c227d5959ffe4ecd30.png)
